baseline.title: How does SmolLM3’s 128k context and hybrid reasoning impact practical use in MistralRS?
baseline.body: An archived post from mid-2025 reports that SmolLM3 is a state-of-the-art 3 billion parameter model with hybrid reasoning capabilities and a notably large 128,000 token context window. It also mentions a performance figure of 105 tokens per second on an M3 Max using AFQ4 quantization. This model has day-0 support in the MistralRS framework, which itself offers features like a built-in MCP client, an OpenAI HTTP server, and full multimodal inference for image, audio, and text. Given these reported specs, what are the practical tradeoffs in deploying SmolLM3 locally with MistralRS? Specifically, how does the large context window affect memory and speed in real-world scenarios, and how mature is the hybrid reasoning functionality in typical tasks? Additionally, how well do MistralRS’s multimodal and server features integrate with such a model in practice? Any insights or experiences with this setup would be valuable to understand its current usability and limitations.
